title: arXiv Trending AI — October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from cumulative Hugging Face Papers upvotes and corroborating signals. Citation evidence is sparse for recent papers, and platform engagement is not a universal popularity measure. Older papers first submitted before October and revised during the window were not exhaustively enumerated.

sections.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
sections.abstract: Jeva treats structured decision-making as a native model task, separating reusable request/option representations from set-dependent choice while supporting null answers, permutation consistency, variable-size candidate sets, and caching.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a decision-native architecture with a separate coverage gate for null decisions and cached option-side computation, reporting near-perfect null detection and no decision flips under tested permutations.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported invariance and null-detection results are bounded by the evaluated models and tested permutations; the abstract does not establish robustness across arbitrary decision tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Papers displayed 404 upvotes at the snapshot; Semantic Scholar reported 4 current citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
sections.abstract: WeVisOne-VL unifies object-level and pixel-level vision-language tasks through structured outputs and a lightweight pixel decoder, and reports evaluations on more than 30 benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors connect structured object predictions to instance-level masks and mattes through an <OBJ> token and pixel decoder, followed by supervised curriculum training and mixed-task reinforcement learning.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that the current model is single-turn, omits chain-of-thought reasoning, and may trade off general capability; clear benchmark prompts may understate difficulty with vague real-world instructions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Papers displayed 258 upvotes at the snapshot; Semantic Scholar reported 0 current citations. The paper reports evaluation on more than 30 benchmarks and releases code and model weights.

sections.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
sections.abstract: VideoJev scores temporal intervals and textual options directly against video evidence, reusing visual computation for follow-up queries; the authors report improved temporal-grounding scores and large inference speedups on video QA.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that cached and joint inference reuse visual computation, improving mean mIoU by 6.7 and 10.8 points for the 4B and 35B-A3B models over their backbones, with 2.8–3.1× grounding speedups and over 100× video-QA speedups in the stated setup.
sections.unique_caveat: The measured speedups and quality claims are tied to selected temporal-grounding and video-QA benchmarks and the paper's repeated-query inference setup; they do not establish the same gains for arbitrary video-agent workflows.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Papers displayed 241 upvotes at the snapshot; Semantic Scholar reported 1 current citation and 0 influential citations. The authors report results across three grounding and four video-QA benchmarks.

sections.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
sections.abstract: MemT-1.0 adds persistent, model-internal memory with token-level updates and Mixture-of-Storage capacity scaling, reporting results on memory and general-capability benchmarks and agentic coding tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce stable Gated DeltaNet-2 memory updates and Mixture-of-Storage; they report that MemT-1.0-Nano at 128K history is 1.86× faster end-to-end and uses 66× less persistent storage than a full-context KV cache.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify a fixed-size memory-state trade-off: constant storage limits detailed historical fidelity as interactions accumulate, and how local memory should consolidate into trainable hyper memory remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Papers displayed 183 upvotes at the snapshot; Semantic Scholar reported 2 current citations, including 1 influential citation. The paper is cross-listed in two core AI categories and reports 11 memory benchmarks.

sections.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
sections.abstract: AgentGarten couples stateful simulators with a shared neural renderer so agents can learn from visual interaction and pass playbooks from one round of experience to later agents.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine code-defined environments, a real-time neural renderer and inherited experience playbooks; their study reports learning behaviors after four rounds in a hide-and-seek environment, compared with millions of rounds for a conventional RL counterpart.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported efficiency comparison is within the authors' simulator-based tasks and baseline setup; it does not establish transfer to arbitrary or physical environments.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Papers displayed 180 upvotes at the snapshot and labels it '#1 Paper of the day'; Semantic Scholar reported 1 current citation and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
sections.abstract: TokenRouter serves token-level LLM routing with request-centric programming, asynchronous model execution and delayed batching, reporting 2.01–64.15× higher decoding throughput than the compared systems.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors separate routing logic from serving execution and report higher decoding throughput across routing algorithms, workloads and model pairs.
sections.unique_caveat: The throughput model assumes a geometric distribution for tokens between consecutive sends; the authors leave corner cases that violate this assumption for future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Papers displayed 144 upvotes at the snapshot. The arXiv record says the work was accepted by NeurIPS 2026 and links code; Semantic Scholar reported 0 current citations.

sections.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
sections.abstract: Hy-Nomas is an 8B diffusion world model for multi-turn text and camera control that carries history across generated video segments using action-aware causal attention and structured captions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine action-aware causal attention, a vision-language Prompt Enhancer and progressive training; on their 280-case Hy-Nomas-Bench they report human-evaluation advantages over selected interactive world models.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors' benchmark focuses on prompt following, physical plausibility, camera control and spatial memory rather than visual fidelity, aesthetics or audio; they also note that temporal causality alone does not ensure physical causality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Papers displayed 126 upvotes at the snapshot after only 2.9 days since first submission; Semantic Scholar reported 0 current citations. The authors release weights, code and benchmarks.

sections.title: Learn2Play Bench: How Well Do LLM Agents Learn from Experience in Unfamiliar Environments?
sections.abstract: Learn2Play Bench uses text games with novel or counterintuitive rules to test whether agents learn through repeated interaction rather than rely on pretrained knowledge, and compares models, harnesses and human players.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that full action-and-feedback histories can help more than distilled rules in their test settings, that the best human players outperform evaluated agents, and that harness changes can improve performance while reducing estimated cost.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark uses text-based games and evaluates learning without model-weight updates; the authors' results do not establish transfer to open-ended environments or show that current agents match human exploration.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Hugging Face Papers displayed 60 upvotes at the snapshot; Semantic Scholar reported 1 current citation and 0 influential citations. Its engagement is lower than the other selected entries; the human-player comparison adds a distinct evaluation signal.
